newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW-Eastman to double Asian sales.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Eastman to double Asian sales.

text.p: Eastman Chemical Co is seeking to double its Asia-Pacific sales in the next three to four years following the inauguration of new plants in Singapore and Malaysia, a senior company official said on Tuesday.

"We are projecting for an 18-20 pecent growth in sales into the next century," Bruce Moore, president and managing director of Eastman Chemical Asia Pacific, told Reuters in an interview at the ground breaking of the company's US$200 million plant.
In 1996, US$548 million of the group's sales of nearly US$4.8 billion came from the Asia-Pacific region.

Eastman as a group is aiming for annual grwoth of 10 percent between now and 2000 and planned to raise group sales from outside the United States to half within the next few years from one-third now, Moore said.
He said the company was raising its fixed assests outside the United States to 30 percent over the same time period from five percent in 1990 as part of the drive.
Eastman also said in a statement on Tuesday it had brought forward building plans for its oxo chemicals complex of six plants in Singapore as part of the plan.

The company had originally planned to build the complex in two phases with three speciality chemical plants starting up first. On Tuesday, the Eastman statement said all six plants would be built at the same time.
The Singapore complex will turn out products used to make vinyl coatings, paints and powder coatings.

Construction of the complex, which includes a 150,000 tonne per year oxo aldehydes plant, will begin in the second quarter of 1997 with production due to start in the first quarter of 1999, the company statement said.
Eastman is also stepping up building plans in Malaysia, where the it hopes to start up a 30,000 tonne per year copolyester plastic plant in early 1998.

Moore said that aside from the plants being built in Malaysia and Singapore, Eastman had also signed a letter of intent with Yangzi Petrochemical Industrial Corp to build two chemical plants in China. He gave no details.
Eastman said earlier it would spend more than US$500 million in China over the next 10 years.
Moore said Eastman was also carrying out a feasibility study in India with the intent of building a oxo-chemical plant there.

Eastman has also undertaken a feasibility study to double the output of the new Singapore under a second phase. Moore said a recommendation for the expansion would be put to the Eastman board in 12 to 18 months.
